title: Exploring Learning Models for Topological Relationship Recognition from Image Data
abstract: arXiv:2609.36172v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Figuring out how objects relate to each other, like whether they touch, overlap, stay completely separate or one sits inside another, matters a lot in fields like GIS, biomedical imaging, and robotics. Even though machine learning has come a long way, people haven't really focused on spotting these topological relationships in images. The main roadblocks? Not enough good datasets and no clear way to measure results. So, we rolled up our sleeves and built a new dataset. It's pretty sizable: over 11,000 labelled images showing all those essential relationships. We ran tests with some classic machine learning models, Naive Bayes, KNN, Random Forest, SVM, and Artificial Neural Networks, and threw in some deep learning stars like VGG16 and InceptionResNetV2. translated_title: 探索基于图像数据的拓扑关系识别学习模型
translated_abstract: 弄清物体之间的相互关系——例如它们是否接触、重叠、完全分离或一个位于另一个内部——在地理信息系统（GIS）、生物医学成像和机器人技术等领域至关重要。尽管机器学习已取得长足进步，但人们尚未真正关注图像中这些拓扑关系的识别。主要障碍在于：缺乏足够高质量的数据集，也没有明确的评估方法。因此，我们构建了一个新的数据集。该数据集规模相当可观：包含超过11,000张标注了所有这些基本关系的图像。我们使用一些经典的机器学习模型（朴素贝叶斯、KNN、随机森林、SVM和人工神经网络）进行了测试，并加入了VGG16和InceptionResNetV2等深度学习明星模型。在数据集构建方面，我们利用分割、轮廓检测和灰度归一化来提取有效的特征向量。结果显示，深度学习方法，尤其是VGG16，表现突出。
tldr: 该论文构建了一个包含超过11,000张标注图像的新数据集，用于识别图像中物体间的拓扑关系（接触、重叠、分离、包含），并通过对比经典机器学习与深度学习模型，发现以VGG16为代表的深度学习方法在该任务上表现最佳。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a new dataset of over 11,000 labeled images for recognizing topological relationships (touch, overlap, separation, containment) between objects in images, and shows through comparisons of classic machine learning and deep learning models that deep learning methods, especially VGG16, achieve the best performance.
